newsitem.title: USA: Canada to seek liberalized trade in APEC - official.
newsitem.headline: Canada to seek liberalized trade in APEC - official.

text.p: Canada will pursue the goal of forging a rules-based trading system out of the 18-member Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, a senior official said on Tuesday.

"We are going to bring further pressure to bear on individual members of APEC to further action plans," said Len Edwards, Canada's assistant deputy minister for trade and economic policy in the Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade.
Edwards, who chairs meetings of APEC's senior officials since Canada was named host of the next summit in Vancouver in November, said facilitating trade is a priority for Canada this year.

Unlike the rules-based systems of the World Trade Organization and the North American Free Trade Agreement, APEC is a non-preferential, consensus-based institution, not a negotiating forum, Edwards said in a speech to economists here.
Commitments are voluntary and there are no dispute-settling provisions, he said.

"For a country like Canada, with only 30 million people, there can only be one answer. We need the protection and security of a rules-based system, not the rough-and-tumble of a global jungle where only the most powerful can survive," Edwards said.
Possible sectors for liberalization include energy products, environmental products and services, and chemicals, among others, he said.
"There are some areas where we can push forward. A number of us are going to be pushing hard on that," he said.

Edwards added, however, that the environment may not be as good this year as it has in past years for solid advances in trade liberalization, partly because countries are about to prepare for a new round of trade negotions multilaterally.

APEC comprises Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papau New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
